case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.

1. Mental Demand

   Definition:
   - how successful you think you were in accomplishing the task goals, and how satisfied

   - how successful, confident, and capable YOU are likely to feel in this decision task

3. Effort

   - how hard you had to work mentally and physically to accomplish your level of

   1 = Almost no effort; you can passively read, accept, or acknowledge.

   4 = High effort; you must compare evidence, revise your reasoning, or justify a choice.
       Example: "Please justify why PE can be ruled out despite the tachycardia and

   5 = Very high effort; you must defend your judgment on multiple fronts at once, or rule

       competing options already qualifies.

4. Frustration
   Definition:

case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.

case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.

case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.

case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.

case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.

case_info.explanation: D.Begin the process of periodic cardiac screening with speckle-tracking echocardiography and radionuclide cardiac scintigraphy. Patients may receive genetic testing, via saliva or blood, for known or likely pathogenicTTRvariants through a variety of approaches as follows: (1) clinical testing ordered by a physician, (2) direct-to-consumer testing initiated by the patient, and (3) research testing as part of a study. Clinical testing companies are required by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to maintain Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments certification and typically report all pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified in theTTRgene. There are more than 100 pathogenic mutations in theTTRgene with considerable phenotypic heterogeneity, ranging from predominantly neurologic to cardiac phenotypes. Hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) is an autosomal dominant disease with variable penetrance for which targeted therapy is now available. The substitution of valine for isoleucine at position 122 (Val122Ile, SNPrs76992529) and threonine for alanine at position 60 (Thr60Ala, SNPrs121918070) are the 2 most common variants leading to hATTR-CA in the US.1,2 Similar to rare variants in other cardiomyopathy genes, the genotype-phenotype associations for other rare variants inTTRare not as well studied given their low frequency. Thus, the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics has created a scoring system for interpreting genetic variants using population databases, computational predictive algorithms, functional data, and segregation analysis (Table).3The ClinGen database provides expert curation and variant classification. The variant identified in this patient (Ser97Tyr) is rare, is located in a mutational hot spot, and has a deleterious effect on the protein function based on computational analyses.4Multiple case series document that onset of disease for Ser97Tyr variant ranges from 46 to 70 years of age. While initial presentation was sensorimotor polyneuropathy, as in this patient, a majority had evidence of hATTR-CA on additional workup, and multiple patients experienced sudden cardiac death. Given the totality of these findings, this variant is interpreted as pathogenic. Although echocardiography and cardiac scintigraphy are established imaging modalities to support a clinical diagnosis of hATTR-CA, data for screening in asymptomatic carriers of pathogenic variants are limited. There is some evidence in favor of screening with cardiac scintigraphy. In small studies of asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant, those with radiotracer uptake on cardiac scintigraphy developed symptomatic heart failure within 5 years.5,6Data from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study demonstrated that Black adults with the Val122Ile variant had impaired left ventricular circumferential strain.7While the differences in strain were small, the ease of use and low risk profile make speckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) a viable screening tool. The 2019 expert recommendations rated echocardiography and radionuclide scintigraphy as “appropriate” in asymptomatic carriers of a pathogenicTTRvariant.8Initiation of screening is recommended 10 years before the typical age at onset and repeated every 3 to 5 years.9While these clinical recommendations can be useful, they are based on limited available evidence. Given that individuals with the Ser97Tyr variant can present as early as the fifth decade of life, screening this patient now with STE and cardiac scintigraphy is a reasonable next step. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is an alternative imaging modality to detect early signs of hATTR-CA. Late gadolinium enhancement, elevated native T1, and high extracellular volume fraction may help identify disease earlier in asymptomatic carriers.10Use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in asymptomatic carriers was rated as “may be appropriate” by the expert recommendations.8 The patient underwent STE and cardiac scintigraphy. Neither test identified any abnormalities. The patient was recommended to undergo routine surveillance testing every 3 to 5 years or with development of any cardiovascular symptoms. All first-degree relatives were recommended to undergo cascade testing and consider further screening for hATTR-CA.
